how_to_play: Open the project in Cocos Creator 4 (3.8.8 per package.json) and build with `cocos build --project . --platform web-mobile`, then open the web-mobile build in a browser.
From the menu (找熊猫 / Find the Panda), tap 开始游戏 to open the 12-level select grid (5x5 up to 8x8).
Tap a grid cell to cycle its state: empty → grass → panda (bamboo cells are fixed and cannot change).
Drag across cells to quickly mark grass.

Satisfy all rules: each bamboo must be orthogonally adjacent to exactly one panda, each panda pairs with exactly one bamboo, pandas never touch even diagonally, and every row/column count must match its hint number.
Use the hint button when stuck (it has a cooldown); wrong placements cost one of 3 lives — lose all 3 and the level is failed, solve the grid to clear the level.
mechanics: Grid deduction placement: cycle cells between empty, grass marker, and panda next to fixed bamboo cells
Orthogonal bamboo-panda pairing constraint (exactly one panda per bamboo and vice versa)
Row and column panda-count hints that must all match
12 precomputed levels from 5x5 to 8x8, generated by tools/generate-levels.js with backtracking uniqueness verification
Tap-to-cycle plus drag-to-mark-grass touch input on a portrait web-mobile layout
Menu, level-select, playing, win, and lose screens with cleared-level tracking
Hint button with cooldown and a 3-lives failure system

rating.reason: Far from AAA: single flat 2D grid-puzzle mechanic rendered with programmatic vector shapes, no audio, no animation/physics/multiplayer/cinematics/live-ops evidence, no deployed build, and no gameplay screenshots to inspect — source alone does not prove playability, pacing, or balance. Most relevant comparators: 2048 (38/100, a mass-validated single-mechanic puzzle with shipped web/mobile builds) sits above it on polish and validation; chess rot (30/100, complete single-board ruleset with flat presentation) is the closest peer; TypeScript-Blackjack (28/100, complete single-table DOM card game) sits just below on systems depth since Find Panda adds 12 solver-verified levels, a level generator with uniqueness proofs, hints, lives, and multiple screens. neverquest (45/100) far exceeds it on systems scope. A 30/100 places it as a complete but tiny and unvalidated logic puzzler at the chess-rot tier.

Include a menu screen, a 12-level select grid, tap-to-cycle cell states (empty/grass/panda), drag-to-mark grass, a hint button with cooldown, 3 lives with win/lose screens, cleared-level tracking, all graphics drawn with vector primitives, and 12 precomputed levels plus a Node level-generator tool that guarantees unique solutions via backtracking verification.

source_analysis.finding: Repository page shows a Cocos Creator 4 puzzle game named 找熊猫 (Find Panda) with bamboo-adjacency placement rules, row/column count hints, 12 levels (5x5 to 8x8), tap-to-cycle and drag-to-mark input, and algorithm-verified unique solutions; no screenshots, homepage, or playable link are shown.

Repo metadata via GitHub API: TypeScript + JavaScript, single commit (2026-04-01), 0 stars/0 forks, no description/homepage/topics, GitHub Pages disabled, no releases or deployments — no publicly reachable playable build exists.

File tree contains only README.md, cocos.config.json, package.json, assets/main.scene, assets/scripts/FindPanda.ts (~32 KB), and tools/generate-levels.js — no image files or build output, so no gameplay screenshot can be inspected.

FindPanda.ts implements MENU, LEVEL_SELECT, PLAYING, WIN, and LOSE screens, 12 hardcoded levels with bamboo/solution/row/col data, cell tap cycling (EMPTY→GRASS→PANDA), drag marking, hint button with cooldown, 3 lives, and vector-drawn panda/bamboo/grass rendering; it registers only TOUCH_START/TOUCH_MOVE/TOUCH_END/TOUCH_CANCEL handlers with no keyboard, mouse-specific, gamepad, motion, audio, or multiplayer code.

Cocos config targets web-mobile in portrait orientation with a 720x1280 design resolution, matching a touch-first mobile layout; its touch events are the documented pointer interaction (README: 点击切换格子状态).
tools/generate-levels.js generates levels by placing non-touching pandas, assigning uniquely-paired bamboos, computing row/column counts, and verifying exactly one solution via backtracking search.

title: 找熊猫 (Find Panda)

fictional_reviews.text: Fictional illustrative review one: a charming little logic snack — the bamboo-pairing twist on the classic grid-deduction formula kept me thinking, and knowing every level has exactly one solution made each win feel earned.
Fictional illustrative review two: solid deduction at its core, but the flat vector look and missing sound make long sessions feel dry; I wanted undo support and bigger boards sooner.

Fictional illustrative review three: twelve solver-verified puzzles, drag-marking, hints with cooldowns, three lives on the line — a pocket puzzler I finished in one sitting and immediately wanted more levels of.
